<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 22.5pt;text-indent:-22.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to SEC regulations, natural gas is converted to barrels of oil equivalent (&#147;BOE&#148;) using the conversion of six Mcf &#147;equivalent&#148; to one barrel of oil.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 22.5pt;text-indent:-22.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The percentage of total reserves classified as proved undeveloped was approximately 51% in 2011 and 39% in 2010 and 2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 22.5pt;text-indent:-22.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Oil reserves represent 48% of the Company&#146;s total proved reserves for fiscal 2011 compared to 29%&nbsp;last year, as the Company continues its successful transition from natural gas to oil.&#160; For fiscal 2011, oil reserves increased 106% on record capital spending and successful completions in the Company&#146;s North Dakota Bakken and Three Forks, Kansas, Nebraska and Texas Panhandle drilling projects.&#160; Because no&nbsp;gas wells were drilled in 2011, gas reserves declined 8%, which is considered at the high end of the normal decline range for the Company&#146;s gas properties.&#160; The increase in oil reserves more than offset the decline in gas reserves and resulted in a 25% increase in total reserves.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 22.3pt;text-indent:-22.3pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to SEC regulations, natural gas is converted to barrels of oil equivalent (&#147;BOE&#148;) using the conversion of six Mcf &#147;equivalent&#148; per one barrel of oil.&#160; This conversion is based on energy equivalence and not price equivalence.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 22.5pt;text-indent:-22.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The percentage of Bakken reserves included in the Company&#146;s proved undeveloped category has increased from 9% in 2009 to 54% in 2011.&#160; The percentage of proved undeveloped (&#147;PUD&#148;) reserves increased significantly in fiscal 2011 primarily because a significant amount of drilling occurred around the Company&#146;s Bakken acreage which proved-up drilling locations on Company&#146;s acreage that directly offset new producing wells.&#160; The Company expects to drill and develop its proved undeveloped reserves within five years of the date the reserves were initially recorded.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 22.3pt;text-indent:-22.3pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bakken reserves include reserves for the Bakken and Three Forks formations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 22.3pt;text-indent:-22.3pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimated Future Net Revenues Discounted at 10% is not a GAAP measure of operating performance. Because oil and gas production is generally long lived, this pre-tax, non-GAAP measure is used by the Company primarily to compare returns on alternative investments. The Company believes that this measure may also be useful to investors for the same purpose.&#160; The related GAAP measure is known as the Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Net Cash Flows From Reserves. The difference between the two measures is that the GAAP measure includes tax effects while the measure used by the Company does not include tax effects. The Company uses the non-GAAP measure because it does not consider future income taxes to be particularly relevant to its investment decisions.&#160; The Company drills new wells on an ongoing basis, and plans to continue to do so in the future.&#160; Thus, it expects to continue to generate deferred income taxes which are not reasonably expected to be paid </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14<a name="PB_14_145642_3020"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Production, Average Sales Prices and Average Production Costs</font></b><a name="ProductionAverageSalesPricesAndAv_143019"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Refer to the &#147;Product Prices and Production&#148; section of Item 7, MD&amp;A.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Productive Wells and Developed Acreage</font></b><a name="ProductiveWellsAndDevelopedAcreag_143022"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Developed acreage at October&nbsp;31, 2011 totaled 23,000 net and 90,000 gross acres.&#160; At October&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2011, the Company owned working interests in 80 net (332 gross) wells consisting of 52&nbsp;net (224 gross) natural gas wells and 28 net (108 gross) oil wells.&#160; In addition, the Company owned royalty and production payment interests in approximately 1,200&nbsp;wells, primarily coal bed methane, located in Wyoming.&#160; In 2011, two wells were acquired, and 22 were sold or abandoned.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Undeveloped Acreage</font></b><a name="UndevelopedAcreage_143024"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table sets forth the number of undeveloped acres leased by the Company (primarily located in the Mid-Continent and Rocky Mountain Regions) which will expire during the next five years (and thereafter) unless production is established in the interim.&#160; Undeveloped acres &#147;held-by-production&#148; represent the undeveloped portions of producing leases which will not expire until commercial production ceases.</font></p>

All of the dry holes were located in the Kansas and Nebraska vertical drilling projects where the Company has historically achieved a 40% to 45% success rate.&#160; By contrast, the Company has achieved a 100% success rate in its Bakken and Three Forks shale-oil and Texas Panhandle horizontal drilling plays.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;text-indent:-9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">*</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the net wells drilled in 2011, 14.2, or 70%, were operated by the Company.&#160; The remaining wells represent Company participations in wells operated by others. All of the dry holes were located in the Kansas and Nebraska vertical drilling projects where the Company has historically achieved a 40% to 45% success rate.&#160; By contrast, the Company has achieved a 100% success rate in its Bakken and Three Forks shale-oil and Texas Panhandle horizontal drilling plays.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;text-indent:-9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Insurance</font></b><a name="Insurance_143032"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company believes that its existing insurance coverage is adequate to protect it from the material risks associated with the ongoing operation of its business.&#160; This coverage includes commercial property, liability, limited equipment and auto, workers compensation, inland marine, directors and officers and excess liability.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Facilities and Employees</font></b><a name="FacilitiesAndEmployees_143035"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s corporate headquarters are located at 1801 Broadway, Suite&nbsp;900, Denver, Colorado, in approximately 5,000 square feet occupied under a lease that expires in April&nbsp;2016.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of October&nbsp;31, 2011, the Company had 15 employees.&#160; The Company&#146;s employees are subject to a collective bargaining agreement, and the Company considers relations with its employees to be good.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">LEGAL PROCEEDINGS</font></b><a name="Item3_LegalProceedings_143044"></a></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From time to time, the Company may be involved in litigation relating to claims arising out of the Company&#146;s operations in the normal course of business.&#160; The Company was named as a defendant in a lawsuit brought by a former employee.&#160; The suit, Pownell v. Credo Petroleum Corp. et al., U.S.D.C. for the District of Colorado, was settled on August&nbsp;9, 2011 at an incremental cost to the Company, net of amounts previously paid, or accrued, and net of insurance proceeds, of approximately $210,000.&#160; The total cost to the Company over the three years of litigation, including legal fees, was approximately $920,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At January&nbsp;4, 2012, the Company had 2,150 shareholders of record.&#160; The Company has never paid a cash dividend and does not expect to pay any cash dividends in the foreseeable future.&#160; Earnings are reinvested in business activities, including stock repurchase programs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As is shown in the table below, at October&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2011, the Company had repurchased 545,429 shares, or 5%, of its common stock at an average price per share of&nbsp;$8.72.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 7.<a name="Item7__162820"></a></font></b></p>    </td>
<td width="87%" valign="top" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:87.78%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .7in;text-indent:-.7in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">MANAGEMENT&#146;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL   CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</font></b></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Operations</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Summary</font></u></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&#151;&nbsp;During 2010 and 2011, the Company&#146;s operations focused on drilling for oil in the North Dakota Bakken and Three Forks shale-oil play as well as Kansas, Nebraska, and the Texas Panhandle. The Company&#146;s drilling activities are discussed in greater detail below.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company believes that its geographically and technically diverse oil drilling projects provide an excellent balance for achieving its goal of adding oil reserves and production at reasonable costs and risks.&#160; The Company expects its horizontal drilling results to occur relatively evenly due to the more developmental nature of the drilling.&#160; The Company expects its vertical drilling results will occur less evenly due to the more exploratory nature of the projects.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In fiscal 2012, the Company will continue to focus on drilling for oil reserves and expects these activities to be a reliable source of oil production and reserve additions.&#160; However, the timing and extent of such activities can be dependent on many factors which are beyond the Company&#146;s control, including for non-operated properties, the timing decisions of the well &#147;operators&#148; related to drilling, the availability of oil field services such as drilling rigs, fracture stimulation equipment and related services, and particularly in North Dakota, the weather. The price of oil and natural gas has a significant effect on the demand for, and cost of, drilling and oil field services.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Certain Significant Effects of the Company&#146;s Strategic Transition to Oil from Natural Gas</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In recent years, the Company has made significant strategic changes with the objective of transitioning its production and reserves from virtually all natural gas to being primarily oil.&#160; This strategic decision was made because the Company believes that oil will continue to maintain a significant Btu price premium over U.S. sourced natural gas.&#160; To accomplish this objective, the Company implemented new conventional exploration projects in Kansas and Nebraska, and new horizontal exploration projects in the North Dakota Bakken and Three Forks shale-oil play and the Texas Panhandle.&#160; These strategic changes are also intended to diversify the Company&#146;s drilling projects both geographically and scientifically.&#160; In 2011, the Board approved a record $15.5&nbsp;million oil-focused drilling budget which was nearly double the Company&#146;s prior year drilling budget.&#160; The following table shows the success to date of the transition to oil as proved oil reserves have steadily increased to 48% of total reserves in fiscal 2011 from only 17% in 2007.&#160; More importantly, due to the significant Btu price premium of oil over natural gas at October&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2011, the undiscounted value of proved oil reserves was approximately 75% of total reserve value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the fourth quarter of 2011, a significant transition milestone was achieved when oil production represented 56% of total production quantities and the Company became primarily an oil producer for the first time in its history.&#160; Due to the Btu value difference between oil and natural gas, oil represented about 80% of fourth quarter revenues.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This transition has significantly altered the components of the Company&#146;s proved reserves, production, revenues and capital requirements.&#160; In particular, the economic and reserve characteristics of the Bakken and Three Forks drilling project are substantially different from any drilling project in which the Company has previously participated.&#160; Among other things, this has resulted in significant changes in the make-up of the Company&#146;s reserves, its capital expenditures and its financing requirements.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">22<a name="PB_22_144237_2897"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In fiscal 2011, proved undeveloped (&#147;PUD&#148;) reserves increased to a historic high</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; The Company&#146;s acreage in the North Dakota Bakken and Three Forks shale-oil play has added significant oil reserves.&#160; The large percentage increase in reserves in fiscal 2011 occurred primarily because a significant amount of drilling occurred around the Company&#146;s Bakken acreage which proved-up drilling locations on the Company&#146;s acreage that directly offset new producing wells.&#160; At October&nbsp;31, 2011, the Company&#146;s PUD reserves comprised 51% of total proved reserves, 60% of which are Bakken and Three Forks PUD reserves.&#160; Refer to the &#147;Significant Properties, Estimated Proved Oil and Gas Reserves, and Future Net Revenues&#148; section of Item 2, Properties, and Note 13 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional reserve information.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost per BOE of Bakken and Three Forks reserves is considerably higher than the Company&#146;s historical cost per BOE of properties being amortized.</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; For fiscal 2011, DD&amp;A per BOE increased 35%&nbsp;to $15.62, primarily because the cost of Bakken and Three Forks reserve additions (both developed and undeveloped) per BOE are higher than the cost per BOE of the Company&#146;s historical reserves.&#160; Going forward, the Company expects Bakken and Three Forks wells to represent an increasingly large percentage of the cost of properties being amortized.&#160; Accordingly, the Company expects DD&amp;A per BOE to continue to increase.&#160; Refer to the &#147;Results of Operations&#148; section of MD&amp;A for additional information.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The significant increase in Bakken and Three Forks PUD reserves in fiscal 2011 was accompanied by a significant increase in the cost to develop those reserves.&#160; Under the full cost accounting method followed by the Company, PUD reserves and their future development costs must be included in the calculation of DD&amp;A.&#160; Seventy three percent (73%) of future development costs at October&nbsp;31, 2011 are for Bakken and Three Forks development wells.&#160; As discussed above, the inclusion of such costs in the DD&amp;A calculation causes DD&amp;A to increase, however, there are no offsetting revenues until the reserves are actually developed and placed on production.&#160; Accordingly, Bakken and Three Forks PUD reserves had a negative effect on fiscal 2011 net income.&#160; In future years, any year over year increase in Bakken and Three Forks PUD reserves will have a negative effect on net income until the reserves are developed and placed on production.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Drilling expenditures are expected to almost double in fiscal 2012 and, for the first time in the Company&#146;s history, financing is expected to be required to fund a portion of future drilling expenditures.</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company has approved a drilling expenditure budget of $30,000,000 for fiscal 2012 which is about double last year&#146;s drilling budget.&#160; Two thirds of the 2012 drilling budget is earmarked for drilling in the Bakken and Three Forks play.&#160; To provide adequate capital to continue the accelerated drilling programs, subsequent to fiscal 2011 year end, the Company has entered into an oil and gas reserves borrowing base revolving credit line with its principal bank.&#160; The initial borrowing base will be $7 million but may be extended twice a year. Borrowing in 2012 is expected to range from $7 million to $12 million.&#160; The financing agreement is pending final execution of the paperwork.&#160; In future years, the Company reasonably expects that additional financing, either debt or equity, will be required.&#160; See additional information below regarding uncertainties related to the timing and costs of Bakken and Three Forks drilling due to the Company being a non-operator, and additional information below regarding projected capital expenditures and capital requirements. See Note 6 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further information regarding debt financing.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A portion of the Company&#146;s estimated oil production for fiscal 2012 has been hedged to assure a certain level of cash flow for debt service.</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company has entered into hedging contracts covering between 15% and 25% its estimated fiscal 2012 oil production.&#160; See Note 5 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further information regarding hedging transactions.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is not the &#147;operator&#148; for its Bakken and Three Forks acreage and is, therefore, not in control of the timing of drilling or the amount of expenditures.</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Larger companies with more experience drilling and operating Bakken and Three Forks wells are the &#147;operators&#148; of the spacing units which include the Company&#146;s leases because such companies generally own a majority (or very large) interest in the spacing units.&#160; The primary advantages to the Company are as follows: (i)&nbsp;larger companies have much larger staffs than the Company which include people who specialize in many of the individual technical aspects of horizontal Bakken and Three Forks drilling and operations, and (ii)&nbsp;larger companies generally operate many wells in the Bakken and Three Forks play and thus have the ability to compete for oil field services and product markets more effectively than the Company.&#160; The primary disadvantage of the Company being a non-operator in the</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">23<a name="PB_23_144313_3020"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bakken and Three Forks play is that the Company is not in control of timing of drilling operations or the costs of drilling and operating the wells.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because the Company is not in control of the timing of drilling operations in the Bakken and Three Forks play, it cannot reasonably predict the timing and extent of drilling costs until the operators actually propose wells.&#160; Accordingly, the Company&#146;s fiscal 2012 drilling budget attempts to estimate drilling schedules through discussions with operators before wells are actually proposed.&#160; As a result, the Company&#146;s fiscal 2012 drilling schedule and drilling budget are subject to significant revision as more information becomes available during the year regarding the actual timing and costs of drilling.&#160; In general, the Company expects its Bakken and Three Forks drilling to rapidly accelerate in fiscal 2012 and 2013 as the operators proactively drill their leases within the primary terms of the leases.&#160; There may be a further drilling push related to development of the Three Forks formation if operators conclude that, for technical reasons, the Three Forks formation should be drilled before substantial depletion occurs in the Bakken formation.&#160; As previously noted, the Company expects financing to be required for its current fiscal 2012 drilling budget, and it is reasonable to expect that additional financing will be required in future years.&#160; However, the amounts and timing of such financing requirements cannot be reasonably predicted.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Results of Operations</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2011, oil and gas revenues increased 45% to $16,767,000 compared to $11,566,000 in 2010.&#160; Total production, at the six Mcf of gas to one barrel of oil energy equivalent ratio, increased 12% to 301,000 barrels of oil equivalent (BOE).&#160; The increased production resulted in a revenue increase of $3,819,000.&#160; As the oil and gas price/volume table on page&nbsp;26 shows, oil prices increased to $85.16 per barrel and natural gas sales prices remained unchanged.&#160; The net effect of the price change was to increase total oil and gas sales by $1,382,000.&#160; Realized derivative losses were $191,000 in 2011 compared to a gain of $115,000&nbsp;in 2010.&#160; Unrealized derivative gains were $8,000 in 2011 compared to unrealized losses of $73,000 in 2010.&#160; Investment and other income decreased due to the impact of market place volatility on the Company&#146;s investments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2011, total costs and expenses increased 33% to $11,854,000 compared to $8,901,000 in 2010.&#160; Oil and gas production expenses increased 25% primarily due to production taxes on increased revenue together with the increased number of operating wells.&#160; DD&amp;A increased primarily due to an increase in the amortizable base including future development costs related to proved undeveloped oil reserves in the Bakken.&#160; (Refer to the &#147;Certain Significant Effects of the Company&#146;s Strategic Transition to Oil from Natural Gas&#148; section of MD&amp;A for further information regarding DD&amp;A changes.)&#160; General and administrative expenses increased due primarily to legal and professional fees and the settlement of a lawsuit.&#160; The effective income tax rate was 26%&nbsp;and 22% for the 2011 and 2010 periods, respectively.&#160; The variation from the statutory rate in 2011 is primarily due to the effect of percentage depletion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2010, oil and gas revenues increased 15% to $11,566,000 compared to $10,067,000 in 2009.&#160; The increase was due to a 38% increase in oil prices and a 37% increase in natural gas prices.&#160; As the oil and gas price/volume table on page 26 shows, oil prices increased to $70.88 per barrel and natural gas sales prices increased to $4.54&nbsp;per Mcf.&#160; The net effect of these price changes was to increase total oil and gas sales by $3,710,000.&#160; Realized derivative gains were $115,000 in 2010 compared to $3,720,000&nbsp;in 2009.&#160; Unrealized derivative losses were $73,000 in 2010 compared to unrealized losses of $1,641,000 in 2009.&#160; During the same period, the Company&#146;s total production decreased 16% to 270,000 BOE, resulting in a decrease in oil and gas sales of $2,211,000.&#160; The decline in 2010 oil production resulted because of delays caused by shortages of fracture stimulation equipment for horizontal wells in the North Dakota Bakken and the Texas Panhandle.&#160; The situation was exacerbated by the expected flush production decline on the Huslig Field discovery which peaked last year at about 365 barrels of oil per day, net to Credo.&#160; In addition, the Company did not drill any gas wells during 2010 due to low natural gas prices.&#160; Investment and other income increased primarily due to the impact of market place improvements on the Company&#146;s investments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2010, total costs and expenses, excluding the impairment loss of $24,653,000 in 2009, decreased 19% to $8,901,000 compared to $10,949,000 in 2009.&#160; Oil and gas production expenses decreased 2%&nbsp;due primarily to decreased field level service costs.&#160; General and administrative expenses decreased $1,143,000 to $2,107,000&nbsp;primarily due to decreased salaries and benefits and lower legal</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">24<a name="PB_24_144334_7748"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended October&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2011, net cash provided by operating activities was $10,803,000 compared to $4,533,000 for 2010.&#160; Net cash used in investing activities was $14,524,000 and $7,932,000 for the years ended October&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010 respectively.&#160; Net cash used in investing activities is exclusive of expenditures included in current liabilities of $3,058,000 and $954,000 at October&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010 respectively.&#160; Investing activities primarily included oil and gas lease acquisition, exploration and development expenditures.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2011 the Company executed the most aggressive drilling program in its history, expending approximately $15.5 million.&#160; As a result, cash and short term investments are being rapidly utilized as expected and budgeted, and working capital declined from $9,661,000 at October&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2010 to $2,940,000 at October&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; Refer to the &#147;Certain Significant Effects of the Company&#146;s Strategic Transition to Oil from Natural Gas&#148; section of MD&amp;A for anticipated drilling expenditures and financing requirements.&#160; Because earnings are anticipated to be reinvested in operations, cash dividends are not expected to be paid.&#160; The Company has no defined benefit plans and no obligations for post retirement employee benefits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, depletion and amortization and write-downs of oil and gas properties and impairment losses (&#147;EBITDA&#148;) was $9,967,000 for the year ended October&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2011 and $6,417,000&nbsp;for the prior year.&#160; EBITDA is not a GAAP measure of operating performance.&#160; The Company uses this non-GAAP performance measure primarily to compare its performance with other companies in the industry that make a similar disclosure.&#160; The Company believes that this performance measure may also be useful to investors for the same purpose.&#160; Investors should not consider this measure in isolation or as a substitute for operating income, or any other measure for determining the Company&#146;s operating performance that is calculated in accordance with GAAP.&#160; In addition, because EBITDA is not a GAAP measure, it may not necessarily be comparable to similarly titled measures employed by other companies.&#160; A reconciliation between EBITDA and net income is provided in the table below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Average production costs, including production taxes, per equivalent BOE of production (using the energy equivalent conversion of six&nbsp;Mcf of gas to one barrel of oil) were $13.29, $11.84 and $10.17&nbsp;per BOE in 2011, 2010 and 2009 respectively.&#160; Depreciation, depletion and amortization per equivalent BOE for the same periods were $15.62, $11.60 and $12.27.&#160; The future development costs for Bakken and Three Forks PUD reserves added in fiscal 2011 caused the substantial increase in DD&amp;A.&#160; Refer to the &#147;Certain Significant Effects of the Company&#146;s Strategic Transition to Oil from Natural Gas&#148; section of MD&amp;A for more information regarding the increase in DD&amp;A per equivalent BOE.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although product prices are key to the Company&#146;s ability to operate profitably and to budget capital expenditures, they are beyond the Company&#146;s control and are difficult to predict.&#160; Since 1991, the Company has periodically hedged the price of a portion of its estimated production when the potential for significant downward price movement is anticipated, or to assure availability of a portion of the cash flow for anticipated debt service.&#160; Such hedges are authorized by the Company&#146;s Board of Directors and they do not exceed estimated production volumes for the periods hedged.&#160; Hedging transactions may take the form of costless collars or forward short positions and are generally based on the NYMEX futures prices at the time the transactions are initiated. The positions are normally closed by purchasing offsetting positions.&#160; Contracts are expected to be closed as related production occurs but may be closed earlier if the anticipated downward price movement occurs or if the Company believes that the potential for such movement has abated.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has elected not to designate its commodity derivatives as cash flow hedges for accounting purposes.&#160; Accordingly, such contracts are recorded at fair value on its Balance Sheet and changes in fair value are recorded in the Consolidated Statements of Operations as they occur.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At October&nbsp;31, 2011 the Company held open short derivative contracts for 6,000 barrels per month covering the production months of January&nbsp;through December&nbsp;2012 at prices ranging from $91.95 to $93.00.&#160; This hedge is expected to cover 15% to 25% of the Company&#146;s estimated oil production for fiscal 2012.&#160; The Company held no open derivative contracts for natural gas.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a derivative line of credit with its bank which is available, at the discretion of the Company, to meet margin calls.&#160; To date, the Company has not used this facility and maintains it only as a precaution related to possible margin calls.&#160; The maximum credit line available is $7,200,000 with interest calculated at the prime rate.&#160; The facility is unsecured and has covenants that require the Company to maintain $3,000,000 in cash or short term investments, none of which are required to be maintained at the Company&#146;s bank, and prohibits funded debt in excess of $500,000.&#160; The line expires May&nbsp;1, 2013.&#160; The credit line has been incorporated into the revolving credit agreement entered into subsequent to October&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; See Footnote 6 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion of the credit line.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Oil and Gas Activities</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Capital Spending.</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Capital spending in 2011 totaled $16,732,000 including $15,500,000 related to the Company&#146;s drilling budget.&#160; Refer to the &#147;Certain Significant Effects of the Company&#146;s Strategic Transition from Natural Gas to Oil&#148; section of MD&amp;A for additional information regarding 2011 and projected 2012 drilling expenditures.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Drilling Activities</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">See Item 1. for a general discussion of the Company&#146;s business.&#160; See Item 2. for a discussion of the Company&#146;s properties.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As discussed in Item 1. &#147;Business&#148;, since 2008, the Company&#146;s business strategy has focused primarily on drilling for oil in the North Dakota Bakken and Three Forks shale-oil play and in Kansas, Nebraska and the Texas Panhandle.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In North Dakota&#146;s Bakken and Three Forks shale-oil play, the Company participated in 8 gross (0.4&nbsp;net) Bakken wells during 2011 with an average 5% working interest.&#160; To date, the Company has participated in 11 gross (0.8 net) Bakken wells with an average 7% working interest.&#160; All of the Company&#146;s Bakken wells have been successfully completed as high rate producers with initial rates ranging from 769 to 3,732 BOE per day.&#160; The Company owns interests in sixty two (62) spacing units with interests ranging from very small to 23%.&#160; The Company&#146;s average working interest in the 62&nbsp;spacing units is approximately 8%, assuming all spacing units contain 1,280 acres.&#160; To date, 11&nbsp;of the spacing units have been successfully tested by an initial Bakken well.&#160; The Company currently estimates that 23 gross (2.7 net) Bakken and Three Forks wells will be drilled on its acreage during 2012.&#160; The Company believes it is likely that more than one well will be drilled on the vast majority of its spacing units.&#160; Bakken and Three Forks wells on 1,280 acre spacing units generally have a measured depth of about 20,000&nbsp;feet, consisting of 10,000 feet vertical and 10,000 feet horizontal.&#160; Wells currently cost about $10,000,000.&#160; Due to the high cost of drilling and operating Bakken and Three Forks wells, their economics are highly dependent on oil prices.&#160; The Company estimates that it needs to realize wellhead oil prices ranging between $70.00 and $90.00&nbsp;per BOE in order to achieve its desired economic objectives.&#160; All of the Company&#146;s Bakken and Three Forks spacing units are operated by larger companies which, thus far, have had the ability to obtain field services on a timely basis and at competitive prices.&#160; See Item 1A. &#147;Risk Factors&#148;.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In Kansas and Nebraska, the Company is conducting primarily a wildcat oil drilling project using the combination of subsurface geology which is generally confirmed by 3-D seismic.&#160; During 2011, the Company participated in 36 gross (19.2 net) wells with an average 53% working interest.&#160; To date, the Company has participated in 107 gross (44 net) wells with an average 42% working interest.&#160; The Company&#146;s overall drilling success rate is about 42%, which the Company believes is approximately the same success rate as other knowledgeable companies involved in the area.&#160; For 2012, the Company estimates that it will participate in 52 gross (29 net) wells in Kansas and Nebraska with an average working interest of approximately 56%.&#160; Wells are drilled to a vertical depth of 4,000 to 5,000 feet, and completed well cost is approximately $450,000.&#160; The Company estimates that it can achieve its minimum drilling economics at oil prices as low as $50.00.&#160; The Company will be the operator of approximately 65% of the wells expected to be drilled in 2012.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the Texas Panhandle, the Company is conducting two horizontal drilling projects and one vertical drilling project.&#160; The Tonkawa and Cleveland formations are being developed by horizontal drilling. </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">27<a name="PB_27_142451_7056"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Horizontal wells are drilled on 320 or 640 acre spacing units and generally have a measured depth of about 14,000 feet, consisting of 9,000 feet vertical and 5,000 feet horizontal. Wells currently cost about $4,400,000.&#160; The Company owns interests in four 640 acre spacing units that are prospective for Tonkawa and Cleveland horizontal drilling and believes that each spacing unit could ultimately contain two Tonkawa and two Cleveland wells.&#160; In addition, the Company has drilled one vertical Tonkawa well and one vertical Morrow well on its acreage with an average working interest of 28%.&#160; It is anticipated that two or more additional Morrow wells will be drilled on the acreage when natural gas prices improve.&#160; Morrow wells are drilled to an approximate depth of 11,000 feet and cost approximately $4,000,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Natural gas drilling in Oklahoma has been suspended pending a recovery in natural gas prices.&#160; Accordingly, no gas wells were drilled in Oklahoma during 2011. Most of the Company&#146;s Oklahoma acreage is held by production and, thus, the timing of drilling is not critical to maintaining the Company&#146;s leasehold ownership.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Reserves.</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Refer to Item 2, &#147;Properties, Significant Properties, Estimated Proved Oil and Gas Reserves and Future Net Revenues&#148;, for information regarding oil and gas reserves.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles requires the Company to make certain estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities and reserves at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&#160; The Company bases its estimates on current information and historical experience as well as various other assumptions it believes to be reasonable under the circumstances.&#160; Although actual results may differ from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions, the Company believes that its estimates are reasonable.&#160; The Company believes the following accounting policies and estimates are critical in the preparation of its consolidated financial statements: the carrying value of its oil and natural gas properties, the accounting for oil and natural gas reserves, and the estimate of its asset retirement obligations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Derivatives.&#160; </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has elected not to designate its commodity derivatives as cash flow hedges for accounting purposes.&#160; Accordingly, such contracts are recorded at fair value on its balance sheet and changes in fair value are recorded in the Consolidated Statements of Operations as they occur.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Oil and Gas Properties.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses the full cost method of accounting for costs related to its oil and natural gas properties.&#160; Capitalized, evaluated, costs included in the full cost pool are depleted on an aggregate basis using the units-of-production method.&#160; All costs incurred in the acquisition, exploration, and development of properties (including costs of surrendered and abandoned leaseholds, delay lease rentals, dry holes, and overhead related to exploration and development activities) and the fair value of estimated future costs of site restoration, dismantlement, and abandonment activities are capitalized.&#160; Costs for unevaluated properties, which typically include lease rentals, geology and seismic costs, are capitalized but are excluded from amortizable costs during the evaluation period. When determinations are made whether the property has proved recoverable reserves or not, or if there is an impairment, the costs are reclassified to amortizable costs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company performs a ceiling test each quarter. The full cost ceiling test is a limitation on capitalized costs prescribed by SEC Regulation&nbsp;S-X Rule&nbsp;4-10. The ceiling test is not a fair value based measurement. Rather, it is a standardized mathematical calculation. The ceiling test provides that capitalized costs less related accumulated depletion and deferred income taxes for each cost center may not exceed the sum of (1)&nbsp;the present value of future net revenue from estimated production of proved oil and gas reserves using current prices (discussed below), excluding the future cash outflows associated with settling asset retirement obligations that have been accrued on the balance sheet, at a discount factor of 10%; plus (2)&nbsp;the cost of properties not being amortized, if any; plus (3)&nbsp;the lower of cost or estimated fair value of unproved properties included in the costs being amortized, if any; less (4)&nbsp;income tax effects related to differences in the book and tax basis of oil and gas properties.&#160; The current prices utilized are based on the average of the first-day-of-the-month prices during the preceding twelve-month period pursuant to the SEC&#146;s &#147;Modernization of Oil and Gas Reporting&#148; rule.&#160; For fiscal year 2011, the average of the </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">28<a name="PB_28_142729_5335"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>
<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='28',FILE='C:\JMS\105455\11-32045-1\task5044174\32045-1-bg.htm',USER='105455',CD='Jan 14 14:22 2012' -->

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">first-day-of-the-month oil price was $86.32 per barrel, and the average of the first-day-of-the-month gas price was $4.54 per Mcf.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in oil and natural gas prices have historically had the most significant impact on the Company&#146;s ceiling test.&#160; In general, the ceiling is lower when prices are lower.&#160; Even though oil and natural gas prices can be highly volatile over weeks, and even days, the ceiling calculation dictates that the average prices in effect as of the first day of each month of the test period be used and held constant.&#160; The resulting valuation is a snapshot as of that day and, thus, is generally not indicative of a true fair value that would be placed on the Company&#146;s reserves by the Company or by an independent third party.&#160; Therefore, the future net revenues associated with the estimated proved reserves are not based on the Company&#146;s assessment of future prices or costs, but rather are based on average prices and costs in effect during the preceding year.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Oil and Gas Reserves.</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The determination of depreciation and depletion expense as well as the ceiling test related to the recorded value of the Company&#146;s oil and natural gas properties are highly dependent on the estimates of the proved oil and natural gas reserves.&#160; There are numerous uncertainties inherent in estimating oil and natural gas reserves and their values, including many factors beyond the Company&#146;s control.&#160; Oil and natural gas reserves include proved reserves that represent estimated quantities of crude oil and natural gas which geological and engineering data demonstrate with reasonable certainty to be recoverable in future years from known reservoirs under existing economic and operating conditions.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As more information becomes available, it is reasonable to expect actual future production, oil and natural gas prices, revenues, taxes, development expenditures , operating expenses and quantities of recoverable oil and natural gas reserves will vary from the estimates, including the timing of expenditures and revenue receipts.&#160; Accordingly, reserve quantity estimates are often different from the quantities of oil and natural gas ultimately recovered and the corresponding production and development costs associated with the recovery of these reserves are often different than the estimated costs.&#160; Any significant variance could materially affect the estimated quantities and the present value of reserves disclosed by the Company.&#160; Reserve estimates and valuations will be adjusted in the future as more information becomes available.&#160; In addition, the Company&#146;s Calliope System is generally installed on mature wells.&#160; As such, they contain older down-hole equipment, such as casing, that is more subject to failure than new equipment.&#160; The failure of such equipment can result in complete loss of a well.&#160; Historically, such data and equipment failures have not caused significant revisions in the Company&#146;s total proved reserve quantities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">One measure of the life of the Company&#146;s proved reserves can be calculated by dividing proved reserves at fiscal year end 2011 by production for fiscal year 2011.&#160; This measure yields an average reserve life of 13.6 years.&#160; Since this measure is an average based on both producing and non-producing reserves, by definition, some of the Company&#146;s properties will have a life shorter than the average and some will have a life longer than the average.&#160; The expected economic lives of the Company&#146;s properties may vary widely depending on, among other things, the size and quality, natural gas and oil prices, possible curtailments in consumption by purchasers, and changes in governmental regulations or taxation.&#160; As a result, the Company&#146;s actual future net cash flows from proved reserves could be materially different from its estimates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Intangible Assets.&#160; </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The patents underlying the Calliope Gas Recovery System are carried as a non-current asset on the Company&#146;s balance sheet and are being amortized over the average remaining life of the patents.&#160; The Company periodically evaluates this asset to evaluate whether the remaining value is recoverable.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Asset Retirement Obligations.</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The FASB authoritative guidance requires that the Company estimate the future cost of asset retirement obligations, discount that cost to its present value, and record a corresponding asset and liability in its Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160; The values ultimately derived are based on many significant estimates, including future abandonment costs, inflation, useful life, and cost of capital.&#160; The nature of these estimates requires the Company to make judgments based on historical experience and future expectations.&#160; Revisions to the estimates may be required based on such things as changes to cost estimates or the timing of future cash outlays. Any such changes that result in upward or downward revisions in the estimated obligation will result in an adjustment to the related capitalized asset and corresponding liability on a prospective basis.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">29<a name="PB_29_142814_5796"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></b><a name="NotesToConsolidatedFinancialState_154153"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">October&nbsp;31, 2011</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">CREDO PETROLEUM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">(1)&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Nature of Operations and Basis of Presentation</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Credo Petroleum Corporation and its wholly owned subsidiaries (the &#147;Company&#148;).&#160; The Company engages in oil and gas acquisition, exploration, development and production activities in the United States.&#160; All significant intercompany transactions have been eliminated.&#160; All references to years in these Notes refer to the Company&#146;s fiscal October&nbsp;31 year.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Cash, Cash Equivalents, and Short-Term Investments</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash equivalents consist of liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less.&#160; During 2009 the Company liquidated the majority of its short term investments in professionally managed limited partnerships.&#160; Other short term investments are directly invested in certificates of deposit and mutual funds.&#160; Short-term investments are classified as &#147;trading&#148; and are stated at fair value with realized and unrealized gains and losses immediately recognized.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Concentration of Credit Risk</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Substantially all of the Company&#146;s receivables are within the oil and natural gas industry, primarily from purchasers of oil and gas and from joint interest owners.&#160; These receivables are due from many companies with collectability being dependent upon the financial wherewithal of each individual Company as well as the general economic conditions of the industry.&#160; The receivables are not collateralized.&#160; In the event that any individual monthly joint interest receivable becomes delinquent, the Company has the ability to net the receivables against revenue distributions, if any, to the delinquent account.&#160; To date the Company has had minimal bad debts.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s financial instruments including cash and cash equivalents, short term investments, accounts receivable and accounts payable are carried at cost, which approximates fair value due to the short-term maturity of these instruments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Revenue Recognition</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company derives its revenue primarily from the sale of produced crude oil and natural gas.&#160; The Company reports revenue gross for the amounts received before taking into account production taxes and transportation costs which are reported as separate expenses.&#160; Revenue is typically recorded in the month production is delivered to the purchaser at which time title changes hands.&#160; Payment is generally received between 30 and 90 days after the date of production.&#160; The Company makes estimates of the amount of production delivered to purchasers and the prices it will receive.&#160; The Company uses its knowledge of its properties; their historical performance; the anticipated effect of weather conditions during the month of production; NYMEX and local spot market prices; and other factors as the basis for these estimates.&#160; Variances between estimates and the actual amounts received are recorded when payment is received, or when better information is available.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A majority of the Company&#146;s sales are made under contractual arrangements with terms that are considered to be usual and customary in the oil and gas industry.&#160; The contracts are for periods of up to five years with prices determined based upon a percentage of a pre-determined and published monthly index price.&#160; The terms of these contracts have not had an effect on how the Company recognizes its revenue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">35<a name="PB_35_150351_5796"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
